insights.title: Dimon moves from positive outlook to peak-cycle caution
insights.summary: In the Q4 2025 call, Dimon called the near-term macro picture positive while flagging geopolitical risk. By the Q2 2026 call he described the environment as close to peak and said management does not know how long it will last. Barnum also described the market as extremely risk-on and said the firm is trying to be appropriately cautious. Q2 2026 results were strong: net income of $21.16B and revenue growth of 27.7% year over year.
insights.uw_relevance: Management is publicly framing current earnings strength as possibly cyclical. Results may be exposed to a market reversal, which matters when assessing disclosure and forward-looking statements.

insights.title: Credit underwriting weakness and cycle warnings grow
insights.summary: On the Q4 2025 call, Barnum said he saw nothing concerning in wholesale credit. On the Q1 2026 call, Dimon said underwriting had weakened and that losses in the next credit cycle would be worse than people expect. On the Q2 2026 call, Dimon described the weakness as mild but spread across revenue assumptions, PIK, covenants and rollover risk.
insights.uw_relevance: The CEO is on record warning about industry underwriting standards and a coming credit cycle. This is relevant to credit-loss and systemic-event scenarios, including leveraged lending and private credit exposure.

insights.title: Buybacks deprioritised in favour of organic deployment
insights.summary: In Q4 2025 Barnum framed buybacks as the low-return alternative to deploying capital. In Q1 2026 Dimon said the preferred use of capital is building businesses, not buybacks. In Q2 2026 Barnum and Dimon said repurchases are an investment decision and not a return of money to shareholders. Share repurchases were $6.79B in FY2026 Q2 versus $8.32B in Q1, and CET1 declined across the three calls.
insights.uw_relevance: Capital return is being subordinated to growth deployment and a roughly $40B excess-capital buffer. The firm's capital distribution behaviour and capital trajectory are relevant to a financial institution's balance-sheet review.

insights.title: Regulatory capital friction rises: Basel III, G-SIB
insights.summary: In Q4 2025 Dimon welcomed deregulation as a plus. In Q1 2026 management detailed concerns with the Basel III endgame and G-SIB reproposals, including a planned surcharge of 5.2% in 2028 against 4.5% currently. In Q2 2026 Dimon was more combative, saying the proposed numbers are falsely done.
insights.uw_relevance: Rising capital requirements and open disputes with regulators affect capital planning and could bring regulatory scrutiny. They also bear on the firm's stated willingness to push back publicly on the rule-making process.

insights.title: Expense guidance hardened higher; card charge-offs lowered
insights.summary: The 2026 adjusted expense outlook was about $105B in Q4 2025 and again in Q1 2026, when Dimon said spending would exceed $105B if every quarter were as strong. In Q2 2026 it was raised to about $107.5B, tied to revenue-related expense. The card net charge-off outlook moved from about 3.4% to about 3.2%, attributed to better-than-expected consumer credit.
insights.uw_relevance: Guidance moved from 'continues' to explicit upward revision on expenses, while credit guidance improved. Expense growth is volume-linked and would be expected to track a revenue reversal.

insights.summary: The 10-K states that PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP has served as the Firm's auditor since 1965. No auditor change is noted in the material provided.
insights.uw_relevance: Auditor tenure is very long and unchanged. No auditor change signal appears in this data.

evidence.snippet: We have served as the Firm’s auditor since 1965.
evidence.source_title: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO 10-K filed 2026-02-13 · Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm

followups.question: CET1 fell to 13.9% at Q3 2026 from 14.2% at Q2 2026. At what level would management change its distribution plans, and what internal CET1 management buffer applies above regulatory requirements?
followups.summary: CET1 moved from 15.7% at FY2024 to 14.6% at FY2025, 14.2% at Q2 2026 and 13.9% at Q3 2026. The Q2 2026 call cited about $103 billion of standardized RWA growth, largely from markets financing and lending.
followups.uw_relevance: Falling capital ratios while RWA grows is the central balance-sheet trend for a bank, and it bears on distribution capacity and stress resilience.

followups.question: How does management decide the pace of repurchases against falling CET1, given that repurchases fell to $6.79B in Q2 2026 from $8.32B in Q1 2026 and the planned dividend increase to $1.65 per share?
followups.summary: Repurchases were $31.59B in FY2025 (0.55x net income) and $6.79B in Q2 2026 (0.32x). Management says it holds about $40 billion of excess capital and prefers to deploy it in the business.
followups.uw_relevance: Distribution decisions made against a declining CET1 ratio shape the capital plan and shareholder-facing disclosure about capital return.

followups.question: What is the firm's capital plan if the proposed 5.2% G-SIB surcharge for 2028 and the Basel III endgame are finalized as proposed, including the roughly $20 billion of added G-SIB capital?
followups.summary: The CFO said the reproposals are worse for the Firm than for peers, with a surcharge of 5.2% in 2028 against 4.5% now. The CEO said the proposed numbers are falsely done.
followups.uw_relevance: Higher firm-specific capital requirements and public disputes with regulators affect distribution capacity and could draw regulatory scrutiny.

followups.question: How is the roughly $160 billion core non-bank financial institution lending book, including about $50 billion of private credit exposure to leveraged loan investors, monitored for covenant, PIK and collateral-fraud risk?
followups.summary: Management reported only one charge-off since 2018, tied to apparent fraud. The CEO said underwriting has weakened across the market through weaker covenants, more PIK and more rollover risk, and the 10-K names private credit expansion and collateral fraud as risks.
followups.uw_relevance: The CEO has publicly warned that next-cycle losses will be worse than expected, which makes the firm's own exposure and controls central to credit-loss scenarios and related disclosure.

followups.question: What were Q2 2026 net income and fee income excluding the $4.6 billion Visa Class B-2 gain and $1.0 billion of equity investment gains, and how are such gains described in guidance and investor communications?
followups.summary: Q2 2026 noninterest revenue was $31.84B, up 46.7% year over year, and net income was $21.16B. The 10-Q attributes the rise predominantly to the Visa gain.
followups.uw_relevance: How non-recurring gains are presented affects the reliability of forward-looking statements and run-rate comparisons.

followups.question: What remediation has been completed since the SEC censure for failing to supervise a statutorily disqualified person, and have regulators raised similar supervision gaps elsewhere in the firm?
followups.summary: The SEC censured JPMorgan Chase and its securities unit over a statutorily disqualified person who traded in the US without permission from late 2021 to early 2024. No fine was imposed, and a cease-and-desist order was issued.
followups.uw_relevance: The 10-K risk factors say prior enforcement history makes further formal actions more likely, so control remediation bears on repeat enforcement exposure.

followups.question: How does the board plan to manage continuity with the Co-Presidents' appointment, CCB CEO Marianne Lake's retirement, COO Daniel Pinto's planned retirement at end of 2026 and Todd Combs' resignation, and what is the CEO succession process?
followups.summary: On June 25, 2026, Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh were elected Co-Presidents, and Rohrbaugh became CEO of Consumer & Community Banking. Dimon described his succession timetable as 'several years' with the board deciding, and the 8-K says Combs' resignation was not due to any disagreement.
followups.uw_relevance: Several board and senior officer transitions within roughly 18 months, with investors probing CEO succession, affect key-person and governance exposure.

followups.question: What are the integration milestones, expected costs and reserve and capital effects for the Apple Card portfolio acquisition ahead of closing about 24 months after December 30, 2025?
followups.summary: Q4 2025 provisions included $2.2 billion tied to the transaction, and about $23 billion of standardized RWA was added. Management said integrating Apple's separate tech stack will take two years and cost money.
followups.uw_relevance: A large pending acquisition with multi-year integration raises execution, reserve and disclosure questions relevant to M&A-related claims.

followups.question: Has management modeled the effect of a credit card interest-rate cap on card earnings, particularly the subprime and co-brand portfolios and the Apple Card portfolio to be acquired?
followups.summary: On the Q4 2025 call analysts raised a proposed cap on credit card interest rates. The CFO said it would present a significant challenge if card became unprofitable, would not quantify the impact, and said subprime and co-brand portfolios would be hit hardest.
followups.uw_relevance: Card is a key earnings driver, and management's refusal to quantify the effect bears on risk-disclosure adequacy in a regulatory or political event.

followups.question: Given the CEO's Q2 2026 description of the environment as close to peak and Q2 revenue up 27.7% year over year, how does the disclosure committee reconcile cautionary commentary with forward guidance and risk factors?
followups.summary: Dimon moved from a positive near-term outlook on the Q4 2025 call to describing conditions as close to peak on the Q2 2026 call. Barnum described the market as extremely risk-on, and Q2 2026 net income was $21.16B.
followups.uw_relevance: Public framing of current earnings as possibly cyclical raises disclosure questions if results reverse.

followups.question: With 2026 adjusted expense guidance raised to about $107.5B from about $105B, how much of the increase is volume-linked, and what expense flexibility exists if revenue reverses?
followups.summary: The Q2 2026 increase was tied to revenue-related expense. The card net charge-off outlook was lowered from about 3.4% to about 3.2%, attributed to better-than-expected consumer credit.
followups.uw_relevance: If expense growth tracks revenue, a revenue reversal could pressure results and the firm's guidance credibility.

followups.question: What is driving net interest margin compression, and how do the 110% liquidity coverage ratio and 5.5% supplementary leverage ratio fit with growth in markets financing and lending?
followups.summary: Net interest margin was 2.4% at Q2 2026 against 2.7% at FY2023. The liquidity coverage ratio was 110.0% at Q2 2026, and the supplementary leverage ratio was 5.5% versus 5.9% a year earlier.
followups.uw_relevance: Liquidity and leverage metrics are mitigants, but spread compression together with balance-sheet growth shows how much room exists under stress.

metric_relevance.buyback_intensity: Buybacks ran at 0.55x net income in FY2025 against 0.32x in FY2024, and fell to 0.32x in Q2 2026 from 0.50x in Q1. Q2 net income includes the Visa gain, and management now frames repurchases as an investment decision, so the pace of distributions against falling capital ratios is a key governance point.
metric_relevance.buybacks: Repurchases were $31.59B in FY2025 against $18.83B in FY2024, then $8.32B in Q1 2026 and $6.79B in Q2 2026. Large buybacks while CET1 declines and Basel and G-SIB capital rules tighten can draw shareholder and regulator scrutiny.
metric_relevance.cet1_ratio: CET1 fell to 13.9% at Q3 2026 from 14.2% at Q2 2026, 14.6% at FY2025 and 15.7% at FY2024, on RWA growth and the Apple Card deal. The CFO expects a 5.2% G-SIB surcharge in 2028 against 4.5% now, so shrinking headroom alongside ongoing buybacks is the central capital issue for D&O.
metric_relevance.equity: Stockholders' equity rose to $374.60B at Q2 2026 from $344.76B at FY2024, a growing loss-absorbing base. For a G-SIB, regulatory capital ratios (CET1, Tier 1) are the sharper test of the capital position.
metric_relevance.fee_income_growth_yoy: Fee income grew 46.7% year over year in Q2 2026, versus 11.0% in Q1, driven predominantly by the Visa gain and $1.0B of equity investment gains. Underwriters should look through this when assessing earnings trends and investor communications.
metric_relevance.lcr: The liquidity coverage ratio was 110.0% at Q2 2026, down from 113.0% at FY2024 Q4 and 112.0% at Q1 2026. Liquidity is adequate, but the small downward drift coincides with growth in markets financing and lending.
metric_relevance.net_income: Net income was $21.16B in Q2 2026, then $15.30B in Q3 2026. FY2025 was $57.05B against $58.47B in FY2024. Q2 includes non-recurring gains, so earnings quality and how those gains are described matter for disclosure scrutiny.
metric_relevance.nim: Net interest margin was 2.4% in Q2 2026, against 2.5% in Q1 2026 and 2.6% for FY2024. Compression in the core earnings engine matters because management is guiding expenses higher while capital ratios fall.
metric_relevance.noninterest_income: Fee income was $31.84B in Q2 2026, against $24.47B in Q1 and $20.80B in Q4 2025. The 10-Q attributes the rise predominantly to the Visa gain, so the figure is distorted by a non-recurring item that affects how results are presented.
metric_relevance.npl_ratio: The nonperforming loan ratio was 0.7% at FY2025, the same as FY2024 and up from 0.5% at FY2023. Reported credit quality is solid, but the CEO flags weaker underwriting and private credit exposure, so any deterioration would test earlier benign commentary.
metric_relevance.revenue: Quarterly revenue was $57.35B in Q2 2026, up from $49.84B in Q1, then $50.17B in Q3. The Q2 peak included a $4.6B Visa gain, so the Q2 level may overstate the underlying run rate that investor guidance is judged against.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_qoq: Sequential growth was 15.1% in Q2 2026 and 8.8% in Q1 2026, after -1.4% in Q4 2025. The Q2 jump coincides with the Visa share gain, so it is not a clean read on momentum.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_yoy: Year-over-year growth reached 27.7% in Q2 2026, versus 10.0% in Q1 2026 and 7.1% in Q4 2025. Management called the environment close to peak while reporting this strength, so how the disclosures reconcile the two is a D&O focus.
metric_relevance.tier1_ratio: The Tier 1 ratio was 15.1% at Q2 2026 against 16.8% at FY2024 and 15.5% at FY2025, tracking the CET1 decline. Continued drift while distributions continue and capital rules tighten is a point for shareholder and regulatory scrutiny.
